pr_title: session, ddl: amend txn correctly when "modify column" needs reorg data with tidb_enable_amend_pessimistic_txn=on.

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/26203 <!-- REMOVE this line if no issue to close -->

Problem Summary:
Columns exist in an intermediate state when we support modifying the column type (which requires reorg the data). So we can't just check the public state columns when we check whether the operation is amendable.

### What is changed and how it works?

Proposal: [xxx](url) <!-- REMOVE this line if not applicable -->

What's Changed:

Use `WritableCols` instead of `Cols`.

issue_context.title: Data may be lost when changing column type with `tidb_enable_amend_pessimistic_txn=on`.
comments:
@wjhuang2016 
The current implementation of transaction amend is not compatible with column type change, in the earlier versions the column type is only allowed to be changed to certain types which does not need data reorgnization, but now the assumption is not true. It's needed to add rejection logic at https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/master/session/schema_amender.go#L163.Also some compatibility test case are needed to verify the rejection.
Seems the column id is also needed to be checked to ensure only field length is increased and other changes will be rejected.

@cfzjywxk 
We have rejection logic at https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/master/session/schema_amender.go#L163. But the state of the column we check should not be public https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/master/session/schema_amender.go#L197.

review_comments: Is this constraint check  `there is only column size increasing change`  still hold for this check function `collectModifyColAmendOps` by now or do we need to enhance it?

When modifying the column type (which requires reorg the data), the column ID is changed. It will return [the error](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/26269/files#diff-e95622ea815b0964b17af236b3d707269eacad4d728fcb52646f22fb33f34bdbR210)  directly.  So we needn't update `colChangeAmendable`. Besides, we use `CheckModifyTypeCompatible` in `colChangeAmendable` which also updated in `column type change(with reorg data)`.
